description: Follows phosphorus from apatite weathering through soil chemistry, biological demand, agricultural redistribution, legacy storage and lake eutrophication, using the Experimental Lakes Area and Lake Erie as evidence-based cases.

related_resources.reason: Apatite weathering, river delivery, ocean sedimentation and geological phosphorus residence.
Lake 227 manipulation, phosphorus continuation, nitrogen removal and nitrogen-fixer response.
Phosphorus excess and freshwater eutrophication; why global metrics do not summarize local lake responses.
Long storage and delayed release in soils, rivers and lake sediments after management changes.
Measured global cropland phosphorus surplus and deficit patterns for year 2000; no global average interpreted as local farm.
1972 cleanup, changing phosphorus inputs, bloom recurrence, and August 2014 Toledo microcystin advisory.
Lake Erie monitoring, cyanobacterial blooms and distinction between biomass and toxin measurements.
